results.context: . Example 1: The Tower of Hanoi Puzzle The Tower of Hanoi consists of three rods: Source (A), Auxiliary (B), and Destination (C). Rod A contains disks stacked by size with the largest at the bottom. The objective is to transfer all disks from Rod A to Rod C while maintaining the proper size ordering. Rules: 1. Only one disk can be transferred at a time. 2. Each move transfers only the uppermost disk from one rod to another. 3. A larger disk may never be placed on top of a smaller disk. Fig 1: Initial State The recursive procedure to solve the problem for $N$ disks is: 1. Move the top $N-1$ disks from rod A to rod B, using rod C as the auxiliary rod. 2. Move the largest disk from rod A to rod C. 3. Move the $N-1$ disks from rod B to rod C, using rod A as the auxiliary rod. results.alt: A problem divides into two sub-problems, each is solved recursively, and the results are combined.
results.context: Divide and conquer solves a problem in three steps. 1. Divide. Split the problem into smaller sub-problems of the same kind. Keep dividing until the pieces are small enough to solve directly. 2. Conquer. Solve each sub-problem. This is normally done by recursion , which stops at a base case : a sub-problem so small that it is solved with basic operations and not divided further. 3. Combine. Use the solutions of the sub-problems to build the solution of the original problem.
